_comment: Rules of the reference check in hooks/tools/config-inventory.py (missing_ref: every path a home file names must exist, so a rename or move can't leave a dangling reference), and the inventory categories that must stay empty. A registry (config/registry/): config/local.json can't override it. Every entry here makes the check look at less, so add one only with a reason; --report lists what each one left unchecked (ref_unchecked).
_note_runtime_tops: Top-level names under ~/.claude that Claude Code or the hooks create at runtime, never part of the tracked tree (projects: session transcripts; state: runtime data the home's own programs keep, such as quota-snapshot.py's usage file state/quota/usage.json; plans and agent-memory: Claude Code's plan files and agent memory, which write_scope.py allows writing to before they exist). A ~/.claude/<name>/... reference to one isn't checked. Any other top-level name that isn't a tracked directory or file is a finding, so a typo in the top-level name fails.
_note_history_files: Append-only records (globs relative to ~/.claude): each row describes the tree as it was when written, so its ~/.claude paths and backticked paths are not checked (a later move must not rewrite history). Markdown links in them still are. hooks/tests/old-registrations.json: the hook registrations as they were before M1 (hook-entry.py), which name the programs M1 archived. hooks/tests/run_worker_baseline.py: the run wrapper as it was before migration step 6, with the flat hooks/ paths of its day (test_run_steps.py moves them to today's layout when it runs it). hooks/tests/legacy_rules.py: the old decision rules of wt_controls.py and auto-merge.py, frozen as text, which name the runs/ files of their day.
_note_absent_paths: Paths (relative to ~/.claude) that must never exist: files the design stopped producing. A reference to one is an absence check, not a dangling path: config-inventory counts it as checked ('absent path') while the path is absent and reports a missing_ref when it exists. hooks/settings-hooks.json: the generated settings fragment of M1; the hooks section of settings.json is kept by hand now and hook-entries.py only checks it.
_note_forbidden_categories: Enforced inventory categories whose debt reached zero: an entry in one fails config-inventory.py and tests/test_config_inventory.py even with --write-snapshot --allow-new, and the snapshot may not hold one. A category joins once its snapshot entries are gone; it never leaves.
_note_third_party_modules: Python top-level modules home code imports that come from an installed package, not from a home file (the standard library is known without a list). Any other import must resolve to a file on that file's own search path: its directory plus the sys.path entries it adds, plus hooks/lib/homepath.py's directories when it imports homepath.
